scope: Prompt/title sampling boundary only; no full factual audit or new task verdict.
prompt:
Arthur is on me for the Q1 instrumentation audit and he wants it by February 16, 2026, so I need to actually do this properly. Last quarter whoever did it just read the status doc and carried the numbers forward, and that is apparently how a few things slipped past us.

I need a clear picture of what is actually happening. For each of our three live titles, which of the events in our taxonomy are genuinely coming through right now and which are not, with the date each one was last seen. And where something is not arriving I need to know whether it ever did, because an event that has never once fired is a different problem from one that was fine and then stopped, and the two do not get fixed the same way.

Do it per platform, not just per title. We cut iOS and Android on separate schedules and the two builds do not always carry the same code, so a per title number is an average of two different things and it hides exactly the kind of stop I am worried about. I want a last seen date for every event, on each title, for the whole taxonomy and not only for the ones that look broken. If a platform is dead on something and the other one is fine, that is the finding, and a combined total will never show it to me.

Fair warning, the documentation and the tickets are both going to lie to you. There is stuff marked done that I am not convinced is actually done, at least one ticket that I think has the direction of the problem backwards, and at least one thing that looks broken this month was us doing it on purpose, so do not write that up as a failure. Work off the arrivals export itself and treat everything else as a claim until you have checked it. Go through the tickets one at a time rather than off the board view, and read the discussion on them, because on a few of them the part that actually matters is in a reply and not in the description.

For each gap I want the likely cause with something behind it rather than a guess, and whether fixing it needs a new client build or can be done without one, because that changes when it can land. Do not assume the gaps share a cause. If two things stopped in the same month that is not by itself evidence they stopped for the same reason, and I would rather you check than tidy them into one story.

Then two things once you have the picture. Any ticket whose recorded state or recorded conclusion contradicts what the data shows needs correcting so the board stops misleading the next person who reads it. And write the audit up and post it where this got raised, ordered by what it actually costs us to be blind to each one rather than by how easy each one is to fix. If something is uncertain, say so. I would rather have that than a clean looking list that turns out to be wrong.
